id_new_fringe_the.blurb: The New Fringe is a small sector of the Black Cliffs, the basalt crags just outside Boise along Highway 21. It sits to the west side of the cliff band, reached by walking in toward the Populace Wall and then turning west. Ten climbs are listed, mostly bolted sport lines with a pair of trad routes, and a few top-rope options exist as well. Grades stay friendly: a couple of 5.7s, a single 5.8, a handful of 5.9s and three routes in the 5.10 range, so it suits newer leaders and anyone warming up. The wider cliffs run year-round, with spring and fall the most comfortable seasons and midsummer quite hot, and they tend to stay uncrowded.

id_ping_creek_wall.blurb: Ping Creek Wall is a low-angle slab above the east shore of Payette Lake, a short drive from McCall. Ten routes are listed, a blend of six sport lines and four trad climbs, mostly one to three pitches long. The grades are moderate, running from easy fifth class through the 5.8 and 5.9 range with a few 5.10 sport pitches at the top end, so it works well for newer leaders or for practice before longer slab days. The wall faces mostly west and gets sun through the afternoon in summer. Cracks here are often shallow seams, though one 5.9 trad pitch stands out for its deeper hand crack and a full rack is wise there.
